This wall shall serve as a fan; when the wind comes we'll give it one sweep, and the wind will blow back, this is called "returning the wind."" The words were not yet finished when Zhu Jiu, the one who had robbed travellers in the road on Mount Qinling, stood nearby and roared out, "If only you can return the wind, then I will go and set it on fire and burn it clean to the ground!" Seeing him so rash, Wang Neng quickly stopped him, saying, "His temple is not yet built, what will you burn? Wait until he has built it, and then there is no hurry to burn it!" At these words all the fellows burst into laughter.

Who would have thought that some meddlesome Daoist would carry these words abroad and spread idle tales to this one and that. As the years passed, the rumor endured and was handed down untruthfully, until it was taken as fact, the tale running: "A monk built a West Wind Temple to scatter White Cloud Abbey; the Daoists used a counter-spell, returning the wind and turning back the fire, and burned the West Wind Temple down." In truth nothing of the sort happened. It was simply that on one side there arose a meddlesome monk and on the other a boasting Daoist. One said this, the other said that, and it stirred up those fond of provoking trouble, who wove it into a saying. Many old practitioners, born and raised in the capital, could never make heads or tails of the matter. Now, corrected after the old books without error, it may serve so that later followers do not contend over strength and weakness, and so bring luster to the law of cause and effect.
Since ancient days false rumor must not be believed; / told and retold, it grows the more absurd;
Men today take it as real and true, / and ever judge the ancients wrong or right.

It is further told that after Qiu Zhenren had made peace with White Cloud Chan Master, in the intervals of quiet cultivation he likened the practice-work of nine times nine, eighty-one turnings, to the eighty-one hardships of the journey of cultivation. Using true nature and original feeling, the heart-monkey and the mind-horse, as instruments of his own use, and taking the seven emotions, six desires, three corpses, and six thieves as outer demons that seek to seize and plunder, he wrote a great book called Journey to the West. When the book was finished, he sent the acolyte to the Jixian Academy to present it to White Cloud Chan Master. White Cloud Chan Master was a man of great wisdom, and knowing at a glance, he too took the sights of the grotto, the subtle functions within stillness, the six times six, thirty-six roads of outward demons attacking the self, and the transformations whereby wisdom and divine power overcome them, and wrote a great book called Investiture of the Gods; he likewise sent a novice to White Cloud Abbey to present it to Qiu Zhenren. From this time the two families were on good terms. White Cloud Chan Master, now complete in divine powers, flew his staff to the south of the Yangtze to expound the teachings there. This one immortal and one Buddha, having authored Journey to the West and Investiture of the Gods, have left them to endure for ten thousand ages, their subtle uses never exhausted.
In these two great books deep mystery resides; / illusion is made by men, a principle that abides;
Within them the seven emotions and six desires stir, / giving birth to demon kings by the thousand, by the score.

It is further told that Qiu Zhenren established a platform at White Cloud Abbey to preach the teaching, expounded the precepts, and opened wide the door of salvation, reviving the Way of Complete Perfection and setting up rules and standards to warn later generations. He also left behind admonitory writings for posterity, founded the seventy-two great monastic forests of the order, and received descendants of the Mysterious lineage for a hundred thousand years. With three thousand meritorious deeds and eight hundred perfect practices, he was due to answer the call of the Purple Palace and attain the rank of a Great Lofty Immortal.

The thirty-three heavens, the cinnabar writ sends down its decree; on the nineteenth day of the tenth month he rode a crane and ascended. At that time, rainbow light blanketed and refracted, purple vapor soared with true energy, golden boys paired to lead him on, jade maidens in twos to show the way. A gentle breeze stirred, and in mid-heaven banners and pennons danced; clear tones rang bright, and within the clouds celestial music chimed. In an instant he left the land of Beijing, and in a moment came to the Southern Gate of Heaven. The kings Wang, Ma, Yin, and Zhao clasped hands in greeting; Zhang, Ge, Xu, and Sa smiled to welcome him. He paid court to the Sovereign Supreme before the golden hall, and beheld the heavenly countenance in the jade palace. Prostrating himself below the jasper steps, he called himself a subject before the Lingxiao Hall: "Long live our Emperor, without bound! Great is the imperial virtue that cherishes life!" The Most High, seeing him, was overjoyed and ordered an examination of his merits. The Three Officers ascended the hall to recommend the Seven Perfected Ones: "His merit is worthy of praise; weighing his bitter practice in internal and external works, Qiu Changchun is first. Penetrating the subtle mystery of the Ultimateless and the Supreme Ultimate, Liu Changsheng is second. Tan Changzhen, his Dao-mind firm, is ranked third. Ma Danyang, pure and still and non-active, rightly deserves fourth. Hao Taigu, unstained by a single mote, is raised to fifth. Wang Yuyang, with ten thousand thoughts all stilled, should take sixth. Sun Bu'er, her wisdom complete, first championed the practice, and her merit is greatest and should stand above the rest; yet to yield a step, let her, who was first among them, now be last, and take the name seventh, complete from beginning to end. The fruits of the Seven Perfected Ones have already been inscribed in the Purple Palace; now your servant dares to report them." When he had finished, the heavenly countenance was pleased, and one by one it conferred titles upon the Seven: Qiu Changchun was appointed the Celestial Immortal Champion, highest rank of those chosen in the Purple Palace, patriarch of Complete Perfection, the True Lord of Miraculous Manifestation and Resplendent Response, Principal Teacher. Liu Changsheng was conferred the Mysterious and Calm, Virtue-Retaining True Lord. Tan Changzhen the Ancestral-Mystery and Bright-Virtue True Lord. Ma Danyang the Non-Acting, Universal-Transforming True Lord. Hao Taigu the Penetrating-Mystery and Marvellous-Extreme True Lord. Wang Yuyang the Vastly-Compassionate, Universally-Saving True Lord. Sun Bu'er the Mysterious-Void and Harmonious-Transforming Primordial Lady.

When the Most High had bestowed the titles, the six, Liu, Tan, Ma, Hao, Wang, and Sun, all rendered thanks; only Qiu Changchun would not. The Three Officials cried out, "Qiu Changchun, why do you not give thanks?" Prostrate upon the jasper steps, weeping and in fear, Qiu Zhenren replied, "It is not that your servant will not give thanks; it is only that the Way is hard to learn and immortality hard to attain. Among those of later generations who cultivate the Way, who like your servant endure a hundred thousand hardships without retreating from their original resolve, not one in ten thousand is to be found. Learning to be good is the hardest of all; without learning to be good, one cannot complete the Way. Your servant has a memorial, "The Difficulty of Learning the Good," to present:"

To awaken to the Way is not easy; to learn the good is hardest of all. For the learning of the good is a thing that only a person of great strength can undertake. One must be able to endure hunger and cold, to bear insult and disgrace. Sometimes a garment does not last the whole life, and food not last the whole day; one goes without two meals, and at night can scarcely find a single lodging. Not a day passes without drawing men's aversion and contempt, and receiving humiliation again and again, to speak of it is bitter, and to hear it chills the heart.'

"Your servant has passed through a thousand kinds of hardship, and so knows how hard the learning of the good truly is. If this single word "good" is so hard to learn, how could one dare hope for immortality? I fear that the cultivators and seekers of enlightenment of later ages, unable to suffer as I have suffered, will bear the name of seeking the Way without the substance of it. Then your servant would have no means to work their salvation, and would betray the honor of the imperial bestowal; that is why I dare not give thanks. I humbly beg you to pardon my offense."

When Qiu Zhenren presented this "difficulty of learning the good" to the Emperor of Heaven, the host of immortals fell silent. Just then a Star Lord walked out from the Western Great Hall, and do you know what this Star Lord was like?

Born with crimson hair, crimson face, crimson beard, crimson heart; carrying golden helmet, golden armor, golden brick, golden whip; his feet treading three-five fire-wheels, chasing wind and pursuing lightning; commanding a million pixiu (
pixiu

, two kinds of fierce beasts of ancient books, used as a metaphor for valiant warriors), slaying demons and capturing monsters. Impartial in his inspection, men called him the Iron-Faced Thunder Lord; responsive as a protector of the Dharma, all reverenced him as the Primordial Spiritual Ancestor.

The story tells that the Spiritual Ancestor nearby, hearing Qiu Changchun's account of how those who learn the good must endure many hardships with no one to protect them, was moved to compassion, and desired to be a god who protects the Dharma. So he called out in a loud voice, "Qiu Changchun, rest assured and give your thanks. If in later ages there should be cultivators and seekers of the Way, should they maintain three-tenths of practice, I will respond with seven-tenths; should they maintain full practice, I shall shine upon them at all times. There will always be those who prepare alms and make offerings, so that he need not suffer hunger and cold." Hearing the Star Lord's words, Qiu Zhenren at last gave thanks, and conferred his respects upon the Star Lord, laying upon that Star Lord's shoulder a burden of several thousand catties.

After a while the Most High withdrew from the hall and the host of immortals disbanded. The Seven Perfected Ones went together to the Purple Palace to pay their respects to the founding ancestor, the Emperor Lord of Eastern Flower, and to the Patriarchs Zhongli and Lu Dongbin, and also to bow before their master, Zhenren Wang Chongyang. The Emperor Lord of Eastern Flower bade Zhenren Zixia lead the Seven to the Hall of Splendid Ceremony to study the rites of the Jade Pond, so that when the Peach Banquet soon convened they would know how to pay court to the high immortals.

When the day of the banquet came, the Emperor Lord of Eastern Flower led the newly arrived true immortals, the southern and northern schools, the five ministers and seven perfected ones, straight toward the Jade Pond. From afar they saw the towers of jasper, the pavilions of jade, the golden halls and silver palaces, with coral for railings and red jade for stairways. Gold and azure light crossed in splendor; crimson and purple dazzled the eye; auspicious rays met the gaze, and rare fragrance perfumed the air. Within the forests of jade trees and jasper woods, phoenixes flew and sang; beneath golden pillars and silver pedestals, tigers roared and dragons chanted. Dark cranes and plum-deer, blue lions and white elephants, all came matched in pairs. Phoenix-palanquins and dragon-carriages, phoenix-vehicles and crane-mounts, none in the world could rival them. One cannot exhaust the majesty of the Jade Pond, nor fully set forth the beauties of Mount Kunlun.

It is further told that the Emperor Lord of Eastern Flower led the newly arrived host of immortals to pay court to the Queen Mother, who received them with the rites due to honored guests. Before long, sages and perfected ones gathered like clouds, and the Queen Mother received them. When the greetings were done, they took their places according to the ancient custom of former banquets, each in his proper order. Only the newly arrived perfected ones awaited the mistress's arrangement. The Queen Mother of the West said, "The newly arrived immortals, before this supreme sage, cannot each pay respects individually. Let them act according to convenience: stand upon the red steps and bow three times upward, all as one." When the Queen Mother had so commanded, the Emperor Lord of Eastern Flower led the host of immortals to kneel upon the jasper steps, and after the three bows and nine prostrations, they arose.

The Queen Mother settled each in his seat; music of the heavenly harmony resounded, and there was song and dance in rainbow garments. The delicacies on the table were beyond words, none of them belonged to the mortal world. Many immortal lads passed the cups and poured the wine; countless jade maidens held the flasks and raised the ewers. Dozens of boys, carrying baskets of purple bamboo, flew through the air and straight up to the tree tops, plucking the flat-peach from above and filling their baskets and their crates in a moment. Immortal officials and officers passed them on to one another, until in a short while the whole hall was filled with them. The very largest were offered up to the Heaven-Honored Great Sage; those next in size were set before the Great Lofty Golden Immortals and the true spirits of the three realms; those smaller still were awarded to the teaching immortals of the Isle of the Blessed, the attendants and guards, and all their households. These peaches are not easy to eat: only one who has practiced cultivation may obtain them. If followers of later ages long for this peach, let them too, like the Seven, devote heart and will, cultivate the Way and attain the truth, and come reverently to the Jade Pond to bow to the Queen Mother of the West, and the peach will surely be granted to you. Eat one and you live a thousand years, never aging, long-lived and deathless.

When the banquet was over, the thousand perfected ones and ten thousand sages each returned to their heavenly palaces. The Seven Perfected Ones followed the Emperor Lord of Eastern Flower back to the Purple Palace. This Purple Palace is on Mount Fangzhu, which resembles Kunlun but is not so great or high. Within it, too, is grass that stays green through all four seasons and flowers that never fall through the eight festivals; it may be counted the foremost realm of the heavenly palace, yet not easy to reach. A verse says:
The cause-and-effect of the Seven Perfected ever flows, / and we but hope that each of us the mystery knows;
Endure the boundless suffering of this mortal shore, / and become a carefree immortal, and wander no more.

blocks.text: Appendix: On Nature and Life

inline.s: Without nature, life cannot stand; / without life, nature finds no hold;
To cultivate both nature and life is the true key; / buddhas and immortals refine essence and leave the world.
How laughable the foolish, karmic breed, / a wanton skeleton in its stupid pose;
dragging their spirit-nature down to Avici, / this is a blow of the staff to point straight the way

Life is formed of the mother's blood that comes after heaven, and becomes the body. To have a body without nature is like having a house without a person. If there is a house without a person, of what use is the house? Moreover, a person first has nature and then life; just as first there is a person and then a house. With nature and life, one has both a person and a house; with a person and a house, one can accomplish a career. Consider the moment when father and mother unite, it forms a misty blend, and this is called the Ultimateless. The father's passion and the mother's intention, with essence and blood embracing, brings it to be.

The Supreme Ultimate is precisely nature and life, taking form month by month. From the two modes come the four images, and from the four images the eight trigrams. When the embryo reaches ten months complete and falls to the ground with a cry, at the first opening of the mouth nature transforms into the subtle soul, life into the gross soul, and they fall into the organs and viscera of the later-heaven body.

The subtle soul dwells in the liver, the gross soul in the lungs. The liver has three flowers and the lungs seven lobes, so it is said there are three subtle souls and seven gross souls. The seven gross souls are governed by the three subtle souls. The subtle soul loves life and hates death; the gross soul loves death and hates life. Why is this so?

Whenever a person dies, the nature goes to the nether courts, and according to good and evil, merit and fault, is reborn to receive retribution. Born and then dying, dying and then born again, such is the suffering of birth and death. For he who bears the burden of being born, it is like flaying a live ox; for the dead, it is like boiling oil poured upon the heart. Is this not agonizing?

Therefore the subtle soul wishes only for long life without death, to be spared the suffering of birth and death, and escape the calamity of transmigration. The gross soul guards the tomb and craves the offerings. When the subtle soul departs, there is no one to govern the gross soul, and it is left to run loose; hence it delights in death and fears life.

The men and women of the world think only of keeping themselves alive, and know nothing of cultivating nature, how could they understand the work of cultivating both nature and life? They little know that life is the flesh and blood of the later-heaven body, and that nothing is without a principle of decay. Hence it was said before: life is like a house, and nature is like a person. A house long kept must leak, and long leaking must collapse. So if a person can repair the house, he may dwell in it long in peace. If one does not know how to cultivate, by long nourishing the body must decay, and long decaying it must die. Since it was said that nature and life transform into subtle and gross souls, if one does not cultivate, and the soul and gross soul fly apart, is that not a pity?

Master Jigu said, "If a person does not cultivate, it is like a crab put into a pot: though it has seven legs and eight arms, it can find no door by which to escape." Confucius said, "Who can go out without passing by the door?" If one gains the practice of cultivation, refining the three souls and mastering the seven gross souls, so that three and seven unite into one great elixir, then a single beam of spirit-light goes out through the great gate of the right Way, does it not all pass by this one path?

If a person wishes to know the first methods of this practice, he must seek out a true master. With the true transmission and the wondrous secret, refining the soul and governing the gross soul, this is the work of cultivating both nature and life.

The people of the world know only the principle of the forward course, in bearing sons and raising daughters; how could they understand the way of the reverse course, which leads to buddhahood and immortality.

When a person comes from the mother's womb and falls to the ground with his head reversed, the original spirit of the prior heaven transforms into the consciousness-spirit of the later heaven; the original energy of the prior heaven transforms into the breath of the nose and mouth of the later heaven; the original essence of the prior heaven transforms into the copulative essence of the later heaven. This is called the forward course.

Bearing sons and daughters is all a matter of the parents' essence and blood. As the children grow up, the parents must decline, how could they know the meaning of the reverse course that leads to buddhahood and immortality? To understand this meaning, one must seek out an enlightened master to point out the secret of ascending to heaven against the current.

Earlier it was said the prior heaven transforms into the later heaven; now we speak of the later heaven returning to the prior heaven, that is, refining essence into energy, refining energy into spirit, and returning them to the void. This is called the way of the reverse course that leads to buddhahood and immortality.

How pitiable that the people of the world are deluded and will not awaken; the wise go past it, and the foolish fall short of it. They little know that the sages of the three teachings, having completed the Way and ascended to heaven, though they have won freedom, grieve in compassion for the people below. And so they set flowing the scriptures to hand down to the world, wishing to teach later generations to contemplate the meaning within the books. The canonical collection of the sages is clear as though uncovered, and yet the benighted hearts of men regard it as no more than old paper.

The Heart Sutra of the Jade Emperor says, "Recite it ten thousand times, and the marvellous truth will be clear of itself." People today know how to recite but not how to hold it; they recite without holding, which is like reciting in a dream. Therefore the Confucian books say, "Thought without learning is perilous; learning without thought is lost."
The people of the world do not investigate its principle; I now set forth clearly the three teachings, and by the scriptures lead them into the gate of the Way.

The Doctrine of the Mean says: “What Heaven has imparted is called nature; to follow one’s nature is called the Way; to cultivate the Way is called teaching. The Way may not be departed from for even a single instant; what may be departed from is not the Way.” It also says: “Looking up to it, it grows ever higher; boring into it, it grows ever harder; gazing at it, it is before me; suddenly it is behind me.”
Mencius says: “It shines in the face, fills the back, and reaches to the four limbs, and the four limbs without a word convey it.”
The Heart Sutra says: “Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, while practicing deep prajñāpāramitā, clearly saw that the five aggregates are all empty and passed beyond all suffering and distress.”

The Jade Emperor’s Heart Sutra says: “The three fine medicines are spirit, qi, and essence.” It also says: “Issue from the mysterious and enter the female; as if lost, as if present; ceaselessly unbroken, firm the root and deep the stem.”
The sages of the three teachings all instruct later generations to comprehend this principle thoroughly, to rise above the sea of suffering, and together to enjoy heavenly bliss.

How pitiable that later people do not grasp its meaning, cannot enter the [school], and instead give rise to slander and abuse, deceiving the sages and destroying the worthies, affirming their own reasoning, giving themselves over to violence, and willfully sinking into the sea of suffering—such are criminals against Heaven and Earth.

I now urge the men and women of the world to turn back and reflect. The Buddhas of the three heavens all have the mind to save people and no intention to rebuke them. Therefore they teach people to refine their essence and transcend the world, to ascend together to the other shore.

How pitiable that men and women in their multitudes are sunk in confusion and never awaken. Their evil deeds pile up like a mountain, their offenses are deep as the sea. In good will we urge them, yet not only do they refuse to believe, they raise words of slander. It is like frost upon snow, cold water poured on ice—the more it accumulates the thicker it becomes; how can it ever melt away?
When offenses are piled up to the full, the last three inches of breath are cut off. When impermanence comes and wronged ghosts come to claim their due, can one escape?

There are some shameless men and women who, following their own nature, do not practice the right propriety, are used to devious ways, and dress alluringly, stirring up depraved minds. Men lure women with their looks, and women lure men; men and women enticing one another, they think themselves clever. Little do they know that in the yang world there are yang laws and in the yin realm there are yin statutes; the yang laws may be evaded, but the yin statutes are hard to escape.

I urge the resolute men and women of the world to turn back quickly, to mend their evil ways and follow the good, so that they may escape and avoid [the consequences], and thereby avoid the wrath of Heaven above.

Continuing from what was said above: the shameless men and women do not practice the right propriety, are set only on depraved lust, crave fine food, take the lives of creatures, and harm others to profit themselves. Such manifold unwholesomeness, heaping up boundless offenses—how can it be escaped?

I now point this out: men and women, turn back and think carefully. The body is the root of pain and distress; the eyes, ears, mouth, and nose are the gates that attract guilt. It was said before that nature and life transform into the hun and po [souls]; the hun and po dwell within, while the eyes, ears, nose, and tongue are without. The eyes, ears, nose, and tongue attract guilt and create offenses—why then should the nature-soul be convicted and punished for them?

When a person dies, the eyes, ears, nose, and tongue are all closed, and the single spirit-soul is led by impermanence before the King of Hell. Before the mirror of karma, good and evil stand clearly revealed, and every deed one has done is reflected one by one, and punishment is fixed according to the offense. The phantom body creates offenses, yet the reckoning is demanded of the nature-soul. Think it over carefully—what an injustice! It is like the saying: he eats the meat, and I repay the debt. Are we not harmed by it? Is the spirit not dragged down into avici?

Avici is hell. Offenses created in the living world are punished in the yin world. For oxen, horses, pigs, and sheep, the nature-soul must go to be reborn. Do the eyes, ears, nose, and tongue come to manage it for you? Think it over carefully—is it not a grief!

Our Buddha, compassionate, fearful that people cannot turn back and lose their human body, has specially spoken these words of direct pointing, like a blow and shout upon the head—truly the compassionate heart of our Buddha.

I too, understanding our Buddha, speak on behalf of the Dharma, pointing out and urging, so that men and women of the whole earth do not becloud their heaven-endowed nature but see through worldly affairs. Fame and profit are like floating clouds; wealth and honor are like a phantom dream. The love of husband and wife must one day come to parting. Though children fill the hall, when the great limit arrives they cannot take your place. Gold and silver, however much, cannot keep impermanence from arriving. One should examine oneself and awaken, and turn back in good time.

Seek out the perfected ones, who point to the supreme principle of nature and life, and receive the practice of refining the hun and mastering the po. Without, accumulate hidden merit to resolve the karmic enmities of many kalpas. Within, cultivate the wondrous fruit and realize nirvāṇa, awaiting the lotus seat. When the three thousand merits are fulfilled and the eight hundred fruits are complete.

Heaven above will send down the elixir-book edict; like a cicada casting off its shell, one soars aloft to wait upon the supreme God. One’s rank is fixed by merit, and there is bestowed the immortal robe of five-zhong weight, the golden crown and jade hairpin, forever enjoying the heavenly peerage. The nine clans and seven ancestors alike enjoy heavenly bliss, never again to enter a womb, never again to descend into birth. Unborn and undying, free and at ease; among the three mountains and island paradises one wanders as one pleases—bliss without limit!
A gatha states:
Borrowing the false to cultivate the real—this subtlety is most rare; refining the hun and mastering the po—this is the true key;
Fearing that people wander heedless and never rest, I point straight and make of it a ladder to the sky.
